headlines: Bank of Japan Governor UEDA said if the BOJ fails to adjust policy rates in a timely manner, market concern about an inf overshoot could push up long-term yields.

Bank of Japan Governor UEDA said the BOJ will weigh market conditions—such as whether the pace of long-term yield increases is excessive or there are signs of impaired market functioning—when deciding whether to intervene.
BOJ Governor UEDA said appropriate implementation of monetary policy and achieving the 2% inflation target can help stabilize the Japan government bond market.
Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said if the central bank raises short-term policy rates, long-term yields may rise steadily alongside related policy measures.
Bank of Japan Governor UEDA said financial conditions remain accommodative.

China International Capital Co: Interpreting stronger rate-cut expectations 【China International Capital Co: Interpreting stronger rate-cut expectations】China International Capital Co says implied rate-cut bets in interest-rate derivatives surged after the October holiday to levels seen before prior PBOC easing. One reason: the rapid fall in government bond yields since late September did not trigger PBOC liquidity tightening. The report judges the PBOC is more likely to ease by shifting the policy-rate anchor—keeping the funding-rate center lower—rather than by blanket cuts to the 7-day reverse repo rate and the LPR. That approach would likely cap further declines in government yields; it probably would not affect outstanding loan rates, though new loan rates could fall modestly. Expectations for next year’s fiscal policy stance remain a key driver of government bond yield direction.
